question: when ENCODE knocked down a transcription factor in K562 or HepG2, did the genes whose compiled rules in that cell pass through an element the factor occupies there change more than the other genes of the same compiled programme, more than genes near the factor's peaks, and more than another factor's assigned genes?
why_network_level: the prediction is about genes the compiled programme connects to a regulator only through its elements: a regulator -> element -> gene path, which no compiled rule held before M1b (0 of 440,589 rules named a gene as its source). A knockdown changes the regulator, not the element, so the endpoint reads the path, not any one rule's input observation
endpoint_exposure: none before this registration: the ENCODE knockdown and control quantification files are undownloaded; the lane read only portal metadata (experiment identities, targets, controls, file accessions, md5, sizes). No lane of this project has read these experiments (searched 2026-10-10). The compiled rules come from AlphaGenome, trained on ENCODE tracks that may include K562 and HepG2 RNA-seq, but not on these knockdowns
population: factor-cell units: an ENCODE experiment of an assay in kd_assays, in a test cell, whose target ENCODE classifies as a transcription factor and also profiled by ChIP-seq in the same cell (the UCSC clusters), with a control experiment sharing a GRCh38 annotation. An experiment is used when (1) the factor's own gene has >= 1 mean TPM in control and <= 0.70 of it in knockdown (>= 30% lower; the threshold Replogle et al. 2022 use for a strong perturbation, adopted here, not ENCODE's), and (2) its universe holds >= 10 rule-arm genes and >= 10 others. A unit enters with >= 1 used experiment and its AUROCs are the means over them. A cell type with a single unit is set aside (it cannot be deranged within its cell)
universe: per experiment: Ensembl genes with >= 1 compiled rule in the unit's cell (symbols mapped by GENCODE v50, protein-coding preferred) and >= 1 mean TPM in the control replicates, minus the factor's own gene and genes whose TSS lies within 10 kb of the factor's TSS
measured: response = |log2((mean TPM knockdown + 1) / (mean TPM control + 1))| per gene, the replicates of the knockdown experiment against all replicates of its listed control experiments
rule_arm: universe genes with >= 1 compiled rule in the unit's cell whose element a ChIP-seq peak cluster of the factor overlaps in that cell (census kinds occupancy_same_cell and occupancy_same_cell_with_motif)
baseline: genes near the factor's peaks, ignoring every compiled rule: the same number of universe genes as the rule arm, ranked by the factor's peak midpoints in that cell within 50 kb of the TSS, then by distance to the nearest midpoint, then by gene id
metric: per experiment, the stratified AUROC of each arm against the rest of the universe on the response, pairs taken only within deciles of log2(control TPM + 1); per unit, the mean over its experiments; the primary is the mean over units of (rule-arm AUROC - baseline AUROC), with a 95% percentile bootstrap interval over units (10,000 resamples, seed 20261010)
matched_control: factor identity: each unit relabelled with another unit-factor's rule arm from the same cell (a uniform derangement within each cell type, 1,000 draws, seed 20261011), scored inside the unit's own universe and response; p = (1 + draws whose mean AUROC >= the observed mean rule-arm AUROC) / 1,001
falsifier: control p >= 0.05: the compiled assignment does not pick out a factor's responding genes better than another factor's assignment does, so the regulator -> element -> gene path carries no factor-specific prediction on this endpoint, whatever the comparison with the baseline
decision: in order: fewer than 20 units -> stopped_below_floor; control p >= 0.05 -> not_factor_specific; else the interval of the mean paired difference: lower bound > 0 -> rules_beat_peaks, upper bound < 0 -> peaks_beat_rules, otherwise no_difference_detected
stop_rule: the run happens once (the runner refuses a second); fewer than 20 units stops it before any comparison with no rule relaxed; a knockdown file whose md5 is not ENCODE's stops it before any value is read; no threshold, universe or arm changes after a value is read

outcomes.stopped_below_floor: stopped before any comparison: {n} factor-cell units met the registered conditions, below the floor of {floor}; no estimate is reported and no rule is relaxed
outcomes.not_factor_specific: the compiled regulator assignment did not anticipate a factor's knockdown better than another factor's assignment did: mean stratified AUROC {a:.4f} for the factor's own assigned genes against a median of {c:.4f} for another factor's, control p = {p:.4g} over {n} factor-cell units; the paired difference against genes near the factor's peaks, {d:+.4f} [95% CI {lo:+.4f}, {hi:+.4f}], is reported and decides nothing
outcomes.rules_beat_peaks: the genes the compiled rules route through a factor's occupied elements changed more on that factor's knockdown than genes near the factor's peaks: mean paired AUROC difference {d:+.4f} [95% CI {lo:+.4f}, {hi:+.4f}] over {n} factor-cell units, and more than another factor's assigned genes (control p = {p:.4g})
outcomes.no_difference_detected: no difference detected: the genes the compiled rules route through a factor's occupied elements did not change on that factor's knockdown by a detectably different amount from genes near the factor's peaks (mean paired AUROC difference {d:+.4f} [95% CI {lo:+.4f}, {hi:+.4f}] over {n} factor-cell units), though they changed more than another factor's assigned genes (control p = {p:.4g})
outcomes.peaks_beat_rules: genes near a factor's peaks changed more on that factor's knockdown than the genes the compiled rules route through its occupied elements: mean paired AUROC difference {d:+.4f} [95% CI {lo:+.4f}, {hi:+.4f}] over {n} factor-cell units (control p = {p:.4g})

descriptives_not_verdicts: per experiment: knockdown ratio, universe, arm and baseline sizes, assay
the rule arm restricted to elements where the factor's own JASPAR profile also matches
K562 units alone, the paired difference and its interval without the control

for directed candidate rows (curated GO direction agreeing with the element's rule): the share of genes whose signed change on knockdown has the sign the direction predicts (activates -> lower, inhibits -> higher), beside the same share among the universe's other genes
limitations: occupancy is not function: a factor bound at an element need not regulate the gene, and a knockdown also acts through indirect paths, so a response is not a validated connection
the knockdown lowers the factor's RNA; protein loss and timing are undocumented per experiment
two to four replicates per arm: the response is a fold change, not a test statistic
ENCODE profiled factors by ChIP in few cell types, so the test covers K562 and HepG2 only
the clusters are ENCODE 3's uniform peaks (2020), not the ENCODE4 set
money: none: no request is sent and no key is read

inputs.path: GENCODE v50 genes, as attribution.holdout reads them

result_manifest.assembly: GRCh38; GENCODE v50 for symbols and TSS; the knockdown files' own annotation per unit
result_manifest.partitions: n/a: the endpoint is outside every training set this project fitted

entry_script.why: argv[0] is a file inside this repository that git tracks and reports unmodified: the commit holds the code that wrote the bytes, so a rebuild can run it. The only clean form
entry_script.forms_are_decided_in_advance: genomeos.manifest.ENTRY_FORMS: one clean form (a tracked, unmodified file inside this repository), every other form refuses, and a form that cannot be classified is 'unknown' and refuses too. Read from sys.argv[0] at write time, never declared

code_cleanliness.counting_path_is_computed: the transitive import closure of this script, computed from the files' import statements at write time (genomeos.manifest.counting_path), never by importing: it follows every import that resolves to a file in this repository rather than only the package, counts the __init__.py of each package above a module, resolves bare imports against the directories the source literally puts on sys.path as well as the repository root, and matches every path component against what its directory lists, so a class name such as genomeos.genome.Genome cannot enter it as a file; not a hand-written list
code_cleanliness.note: several lanes work in this one checkout. A file under foreign_uncommitted_code belongs to another lane; this lane did not write it and did not commit it. The counting path is the computed closure above, so a foreign file outside it cannot have entered a number here, and foreign_uncommitted_code_on_the_counting_path names any that could

revision_stamps.sampled: code_cleanliness.git_sha is read while the writer computes; code.git_sha is read when the result is written. Both are HEAD of the same checkout at two moments
revision_stamps.reading: no revision race: both stamps record c267869

traced_inputs.note: Every file this writer opened for reading under data/ was recorded by an audit hook on the "open" event, canonicalised through data/'s links so one file has one spelling, and compared against the inputs the manifest declares; a member of a declared group counts as declared and hashed on its own, a file under a declared directory counts as declared by prefix. The hook is per interpreter, so a file read by a subprocess is not in this record, nor is one reached through a path that canonicalises to neither this checkout's data/ nor one of its link targets.
